draft.title: Factorising non-monic quadratics
card: A non-monic quadratic has the form \(ax^{2} + bx + c\) with \(a \ne 1\). To factorise it, find two numbers that multiply to \(ac\) and add to \(b\).
Use those two numbers to split the middle term into two terms. Then factorise the four terms in pairs, taking out a common factor from each pair.
Factorise \(6x^{2} + 11x + 3\). Here \(ac = 18\) and \(b = 11\). The numbers are 9 and 2, since \(9 \times 2 = 18\) and \(9 + 2 = 11\).
Split: \(6x^{2} + 9x + 2x + 3\). Pair: \(3x(2x + 3) + 1(2x + 3)\). Both pairs share \((2x + 3)\), so the answer is \((2x + 3)(3x + 1)\).
draft.remember: Find two numbers that multiply to \(ac\) and add to \(b\), split the middle, then factorise in pairs.

a.q: To factorise \(2x^{2} + 7x + 6\) by splitting the middle term, which two numbers are used?
a.why: Here \(ac = 12\) and \(b = 7\). The numbers 3 and 4 multiply to 12 and add to 7. The pair 2 and 6 multiplies to 12, but adds to 8, not 7.

b.q: Which is the factorised form of \(3x^{2} - 10x + 8\)?
b.why: Here \(ac = 24\) and \(b = -10\), so the numbers are \(-6\) and \(-4\). Split: \(3x^{2} - 6x - 4x + 8 = 3x(x - 2) - 4(x - 2)\), which gives \((3x - 4)(x - 2)\). Expanding \((3x - 2)(x - 4)\) gives a middle term of \(-14x\), so it is wrong.
b.clue: The numbers multiply to 24 and add to a negative number.
